headline: All majors underwater on the 200-day line; whales moving coins to cold storage while funding stays expensive and longs crowd the boat.
paragraphs: The regime is bear across the board. Bitcoin sits at 63,498, down 49.1 percent from its 12-month high of 124,740, and trades below its 200-day simple moving average with no golden cross in sight. Ethereum is worse: 60.9 percent off its 12-month peak at 4,818, also below the 200-day line. Ethereum is actually flat to slightly negative over the past 24 hours at 0.05 percent gain despite a 19.85 percent bounce over the past 30 days. The minor alts follow: Solana is 69.5 percent down from its high and 30 days in the green, but today it fell 0.82 percent and remains submerged. XRP, BNB, and Doge are all below their 200-day lines as well. Only Cardano at 0.1813 shows any unusual move, up 25.73 percent in a month but down 3.02 percent today and still 81.2 percent below its high. This is not a market showing strength at the trend level; it is a market in a drawn-out downtrend with scattered tactical bounces.

The momentum picture is fractured and weak. Bitcoin's RSI of 45.9 sits below neutral (50), its MACD is below signal, and the 24-hour move of negative 0.06 percent says the bounce is stalling. Ethereum's RSI at 51.2 is barely neutral; its MACD is also below signal. The sell-side is not decisively pressing, but neither is the buy-side driving. BNB and Solana are outliers here: BNB's RSI sits at 63.4, a clear overbought condition for a coin with no uptrend to support it, and its MACD is above signal. Solana's RSI is 52.3 with MACD above signal, a divergence between overbought momentum conditions and an asset 69.5 percent below its 12-month high and still trading below the 200-day line. These two show localized momentum strength, but that momentum is occurring in a bear regime. XRP tells a harsher story: RSI at 35.7, MACD below signal, and down 7.34 percent over the past week. When momentum weakens into oversold territory during a downtrend, bounces are fragile.

Leverage positioning reveals a market tilted long and paying to hold that bet. Bitcoin open interest sits at 2.12 billion dollars with a long-to-short ratio of 1.86, meaning nearly twice as much notional exposure is betting up. Its funding rate runs at 0.01 percent per eight-hour interval, or 11 percent annualized, which is not extreme but is positive: longs are paying shorts to hold their positions. Over the past 24 hours, Bitcoin saw 617 liquidations totaling 3.7 million dollars, with long liquidations at 2.51 million and shorts at 1.19 million. That is a 2.1-to-1 ratio of long wipe-outs to short wipe-outs. Ethereum follows the same pattern: 1.27 billion in open interest, long-to-short ratio of 1.74, and 11 percent annual funding. Its 24-hour liquidations swung in reverse, though: 4.21 million in longs liquidated versus 5.96 million in shorts. XRP shows the most crowded setup: 87 million in open interest with a 3.33-to-1 long-short ratio and 11 percent funding, yet only 81 liquidations in 19 hours. Doge is the extreme: 4.93 longs per short at 80 million open interest, with 466,877 dollars in long liquidations versus 150,882 in shorts. These long-heavy setups with persistent funding are expensive bets; a sudden sell-off would unwind them fast.

Whale behavior and spot inflows paint a story of accumulation into weakness. Over the past 48 hours, 236.9 million dollars in notional value moved off exchanges, with Bitcoin accounting for 180.8 million and Ethereum for 56.1 million. This is not retail panic selling; these are large holders moving coins to self-custody or cold storage. The biggest single moves: 128.8 million in Bitcoin leaving Kraken, 56.1 million in Ethereum leaving Binance, and 169.8 million in Tether leaving Bitfinex. In the five-session average, whale flows have been volatile: plus 1.14 billion, plus 1.21 billion, minus 777 million, and now this current 48-hour move. The picture is one of rotation and accumulation at tactical lows rather than capitulation. On the spot side, Bitcoin ETF flows show 7.8 million in net inflow on August 11 (the latest date), but only one day in the same direction; the five-session cumulative is positive at 346.9 million. Ethereum ETF flows are smaller at minus 1.7 million on the day, with two days same-direction, and a five-session net of plus 186.2 million. Stablecoin float stands at 306.4 billion, down 0.98 percent over the past 30 days, which suggests dry powder is not increasing materially, even as coins move off exchange.

Sentiment sits at 27 on the Fear and Greed Index, firmly in fear territory and within a 30-day range of 22 to 33. This is consistent with the technical picture: a market in a bear regime with weak momentum, expensive long leverage, and investors feeling uneasy. What is notable is that despite the fear, whales are buying, not selling into the fear, and spot ETF flows remain positive on the five-day horizon. The mood and the money flows are not yet synchronized into a capitulation low, but they are not synchronized into a rally either. The regime remains bearish, the crowd is frightened, and large players are accumulating. The tension to watch is whether the expensive long positioning at Bitcoin (1.86-to-1 long-short ratio at 11 percent funding) and the crowded Doge setup (4.93-to-1 with 9.5 percent funding) hold if price tests lower support, or whether the whale accumulation and positive ETF momentum force a mean reversion higher. Bitcoin's reclaim of its 200-day line, currently around 59,500, would be the clearest sign that the tape's underlying strength is shifting the regime.

The Bitcoin network shows normal cost with difficulty falling: fastest and typical fees are both 1 sat per byte, and difficulty is down 3.9 percent with 1,450 blocks until retarget. This means the network is not congested and miner pressure is not building. The top movers show scattered retail interest: BTW up 25.4 percent, VIRTUAL up 12.2 percent, and UNI down 4.8 percent. These are not signals from the majors. The read remains that the majors are in a bear trend with overbought momentum pockets, expensive long leverage, whales accumulating, and the crowd in fear. The specific condition to monitor is the holding or breaking of Bitcoin's open interest at 2.12 billion dollars combined with a funding rate flip from positive to negative, which would signal shorts gaining confidence, or a break above the 200-day line with MACD crossing back above signal, which would mark a regime shift to recovery.
